cells.tense: You are standing in the clear space where a false structure has already fallen.
cells.ask: With the person in front of you, say one thing plainly that the two of you have been talking around. Then let a full minute pass without filling it.
cells.core:
A thing built on a wrong assumption is coming apart, and you are neither ahead of it nor behind it. A premise is losing its grip and you are watching that without calling it disaster. What is falling was pressing on the people near you anyway, so its going takes weight off the room.

Watch how you handle it. Someone tells you what they actually feel, and nothing in you races to defend the old arrangement. They get to be different from you and still be met. The fixing isn't the point, and there's nothing to hurry. What ends, ends where both of you can hear it, and you stand in the space it leaves.
cells.sheetLine: You are letting false things fall, with someone beside you.
cells.place: in the connection between you and someone close

cells.tense: You are tearing down what belongs to a future that has not arrived.
cells.ask: Pick one bond that's steady and leave it untouched for a week. Don't fix it, don't test it, just notice what your hands want to do.
cells.core:
The clarity is real, and it has gotten ahead of what is actually here. Openings that could wait get turned into things to expose, and the exposing starts to run on its own momentum. What was a response to something false becomes a habit of pulling down, and the people near you start bracing for the next thing you notice.

Watch how you handle it. You can sit across from someone and let their way of doing it stand without ruling on it. Feeling with them is not the same as agreeing, and it is not a verdict either. The bond you have not touched yet is whole today. It does not need your hands on it, and leaving it alone is something you can actually do.
cells.sheetLine: You are pulling things down before they have had a chance.
cells.place: in the connection between you and someone close

cells.tense: Your arms are where they were, under a shape that has already fallen.
cells.ask: Tell the person you've been managing that you're stepping back from one part of it. Name the part, then let them answer without softening what they say.
cells.core:
Something has already dropped and your arms are still in the old position. The effort doesn't show anywhere, and it takes the attention you would otherwise spend on whoever is in front of you. You are in the room, but you are holding up a shape, and the person near you gets what's left over.

Watch how you handle it. Pick one piece of the old arrangement and put it down where someone can see you do it. Let them hear it plainly and let their reaction be theirs. You don't have to set down everything at once. One piece is enough for today, and whoever is across from you gets the attention that frees up.

cells.tense: You are steering through a room whose walls have quietly started to give.
cells.ask: Ask the person closest to you what they've noticed shifting lately. Don't correct them. Write down one sentence of what they say.
cells.core:
A bond you count on is losing its old outline and you are still describing it the way it was. Call it normal, call it a phase, call it the usual way between you — the clearing is already showing in how the two of you talk, where the talking goes, what doesn't get said. The directions you give yourself come from a picture that no longer matches.

Watch how you handle it. Someone describes a change and you let it land without editing it into nothing. What they saw is allowed to be true, even when it is about you. Hearing it doesn't obligate you to agree with any of it. It just sets the picture back where both of you can look at it.
cells.sheetLine: Things are already moving. You have not said so yet.
cells.place: in the connection between you and someone close
